template.title: Episode planning
template.description: Split the source into episodes with a title, end hook, and end anchor for each; drama also includes story beats and a next-episode teaser.

slots.content_mode: Content-mode axis value (drama / narration), used to resolve named variant fragments
slots.source_kind: Source-kind axis value (novel / screenplay), used to resolve named variant fragments
slots.unit_noun: Reading-unit noun (characters / words), following the source language
slots.target_volume: Target volume per episode, an object with all keys {units, seconds, units_per_second}; seconds and units_per_second are populated only when converted from target episode duration, and the speaking rate is formatted as text; null if not set
slots.max_episodes: Maximum episodes to plan in this batch, derived from the text model’s output limit
slots.context_entries: Last few planned episodes, objects with all keys {episode, title, hook}, with null title when absent; empty list if none
slots.progress: Overall progress, an object with all keys {planned_count, remaining_units, window_units}; supplied only with additional instructions, otherwise null
slots.window_is_final: Whether this window contains the full source’s ending (or the end of the unsplit source range being planned)
slots.followed_by_episode: An already planned episode immediately follows this window’s end (true when planning an unsplit source range and this window includes its ending)
slots.failure: Reasons the previous output failed validation; null on the first round

partials.name: text/episode_plan/intro/novel
partials.source:
You are a short-video episode planner. Split the original novel excerpt below into episodes, each with a complete plot arc,
and leave a hook at each episode’s end that makes viewers want to watch the next one.

partials.name: text/episode_plan/intro/screenplay
partials.source: You are a short-video episode planner. Below is an excerpt from the author’s finished screenplay. Respect the author’s episode divisions: extract them rather than splitting again.

partials.name: text/episode_plan/lists/context_entries
text/episode_plan/author_division_rule/screenplay
partials.source: - If the screenplay already has episode divisions, retain the author’s divisions: an episode contains all text from its opening up to the next episode’s opening. Everything the author places between those openings belongs to the earlier episode. Set end_anchor to a verbatim passage at the end of that text; take title / hook from the screenplay too (the author’s explicit episode title and end hook). If the screenplay has no episode divisions, split by complete plot arcs, with each episode forming a complete story segment.

partials.name: text/episode_plan/outline_rule/drama/novel
partials.source: - Also provide story_beats (the ordered list of this episode’s story beats) and next_episode_teaser (a teaser for the next episode; null is allowed for the last episode if what follows is unknown).

partials.name: text/episode_plan/outline_rule/drama/screenplay
partials.source: - Also provide story_beats (the ordered list of this episode’s story beats) and next_episode_teaser (a teaser for the next episode; null is allowed for the last episode if what follows is unknown). If the screenplay explicitly provides beats / a next-episode teaser, copy their original wording; otherwise derive them yourself.
